title: Anthropic finds robots can do many physical tasks but rarely beat human cost
friendlyTitle: Robots can do many tasks, but people are still cheaper for almost all of them
summary: Anthropic’s robot exposure index estimates that current robots can perform 74% of physical US job tasks, usually in controlled settings, but are cost-competitive for only 0.3% of tasks. Driving and warehouse work rank as more exposed than nursing and general repair, where unpredictable environments and dexterity remain major barriers.
friendlySummary: Anthropic estimates that robots can perform many physical tasks in the right setting. Today, they cost less than people for only a very small share of work.
whyItMatters: Capability demos do not tell a business whether automation is economical in its real workplace. Teams evaluating robotics should model the environment, reliability and full operating cost task by task rather than treating a technically possible action as a deployable replacement.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A robot demo is not a business case. Check the real workplace, reliability and total cost before deciding to automate a task.
